Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $\mathbf{v}$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ find $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}).$

e-5434.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v})=T\cdot \mathbf{v},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ -6 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}27 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 2$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}(-6)\cdot x+4\cdot y \\ 5\cdot x+(-3)\cdot y\end{aligned}].

$$
[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-6x+4y \\ 5x-3y\end{aligned}].
$$

    Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}y \\ x\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 2$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0\cdot x+1\cdot y \\ 1\cdot x+0\cdot y\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}y \\ x\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x \\ x-y\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 2$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2\cdot x+0\cdot y \\ 1\cdot x+(-1)\cdot y\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2x \\ x-y\end{aligned}].
$$

    Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 5
?

Find the standard matrix that represents the linear transformation T, whereT:[xy]⟶[2xx−y].

a
[211−1].
b
[201−1].
c
[100−1].
d
[21−11].
e
[201−2].
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We require a 2×2 matrix T such that T⋅[xy]=[2⋅x+0⋅y1⋅x+(−1)⋅y].

Notice that [201−1]⋅[xy]=[2xx−y]. Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation T is [201−1].

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation
content.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x \\ x-y\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 2$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2\cdot x+0\cdot y \\ 1\cdot x+(-1)\cdot y\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2x \\ x-y\end{aligned}].
$$

    Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

before.html:
Question 6
?

What is the linear transformation T whose standard matrix is T=[1010−111−10]?

a
T:[xyz]⟶[x+zx+yy−z]
b
T:[xyz]⟶[x+z−y+zx−y]
c
T:[xyz]⟶[x−zx+yy−z]
d
T:[xyz]⟶[x−z−y−zx+y]
e
T:[xyz]⟶[x+z−y−zx+y]
Submit

decision.explanation: Multiplying each matrix row by (x,y,z)^T gives x+z, -y+z, and x-y, respectively. These are exactly the coordinates in option b.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
What is the linear transformation $T$ whose standard matrix is 
$T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
Consider a general vector $\,[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}].$ Multiplying by the matrix $T,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}x+z \\ -y+z \\ x-y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\,T\,$ is given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+z \\ -y+z \\ x-y\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 6

What is the linear transformation T whose standard matrix is T=[1010−111−10]?

a
T:[xyz]⟶[x+zx+yy−z]
b
T:[xyz]⟶[x+z−y+zx−y]
c
T:[xyz]⟶[x−zx+yy−z]
d
T:[xyz]⟶[x−z−y−zx+y]
e
T:[xyz]⟶[x+z−y−zx+y]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Consider a general vector [xyz]. Multiplying by the matrix T, we have

T⋅[xyz]=[1010−111−10]⋅[xyz]=[x+z−y+zx−y].

Therefore, the linear transformation T is given by

T:[xyz]⟶[x+z−y+zx−y].

content.knowledge_point: Determining a Linear Transformation Given its Standard Matrix
content.problem:
What is the linear transformation $T$ whose standard matrix is 
$T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
Consider a general vector $\,[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}].$ Multiplying by the matrix $T,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}x+z \\ -y+z \\ x-y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\,T\,$ is given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+z \\ -y+z \\ x-y\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 8
?

What is the linear transformation T whose standard matrix is T=[−48−32]?

a
T:[xy]⟶[−8x+4y−3x+2y]
b
T:[xy]⟶[−4x+yx+2y]
c
T:[xy]⟶[4x−8y3x−2y]
d
T:[xy]⟶[−4x+8y−2x+3y]
e
T:[xy]⟶[−4x+8y−3x+2y]
Submit

decision.explanation: Multiplying the matrix by (x,y)^T gives (-4x+8y,-3x+2y)^T, which matches option e.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: What is the linear transformation $T$ whose standard matrix is $T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
Consider a general vector $\,[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].$ Multiplying by the matrix $T,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4x+8y \\ -3x+2y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\,T\,$ is given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-4x+8y \\ -3x+2y\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

Consider a general vector [xy]. Multiplying by the matrix T, we have

content.knowledge_point: Determining a Linear Transformation Given its Standard Matrix
content.problem: What is the linear transformation $T$ whose standard matrix is $T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
Consider a general vector $\,[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].$ Multiplying by the matrix $T,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4x+8y \\ -3x+2y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\,T\,$ is given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-4x+8y \\ -3x+2y\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Transformation Given its Standard Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T,$ find $T(v).$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 7 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The row products are -2+16+2=16, 5+4-6=3, and -1+12-8=3. Thus T(v)=(16,3,3)^T, which is option d.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T,$ find $T(v).$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Transformation Given its Standard Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T,$ find $T(v).$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, rewrite the order of the variables in the usual way:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-3x+9y \\ 6x+y\end{aligned}]
$$

We require a $2\times 2$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3x+9y \\ 6x+y\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 \\ 6 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3x+9y \\ 6x+y\end{aligned}].
$$

    Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 \\ 6 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 17
after.problem:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2y-5z+x \\ z-y+3x \\ -z-2x+3y\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, rewrite the order of the variables in the usual way:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}]
$$

We require a $3\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 17
?

Find the standard matrix that represents the linear transformation T, where T:[xyz]⟶[2y−5z+xz−y+3x−z−2x+3y].

a
[12−53−11−1−23]
b
[2−513−11−23−1]
c
[2−511−11−1−23]
d
[12−51−13−23−1]
e
[12−53−11−23−1]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, rewrite the order of the variables in the usual way:

T:[xyz]⟶[x+2y−5z3x−y+z−2x+3y−z]

We require a 3×3 matrix T such that

T⋅[xyz]=[x+2y−5z3x−y+z−2x+3y−z].

Notice that

[12−53−11−23−1]⋅[xyz]=[x+2y−5z3x−y+z−2x+3y−z].

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation T is

[12−53−11−23−1].

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation With Rearranging
content.problem:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2y-5z+x \\ z-y+3x \\ -z-2x+3y\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, rewrite the order of the variables in the usual way:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}]
$$

We require a $3\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 18
after.problem:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}3y+x \\ y-x\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, rewrite the order of the variables in the usual way:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+3y \\ -x+y\end{aligned}]
$$

We require a $2\times 2$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x+3y \\ -x+y\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x+3y \\ -x+y\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
